quarterly_data.signal: CFO Lorenzo Grandi on Q1 2026: year-over-year, Analog products, MEMS and Sensors +23.2% (mainly imaging and MEMS), Power and Discrete -1.8%, Embedded Processing +31.3% (general purpose MCU), RF & Optical Communications +33.9%; sales to OEMs +24.5% and distribution +19.2%. Gross profit $1.05 billion (+24.3% YoY); gross margin +40 basis points YoY on lower unused capacity charges and better mix, -140 basis points sequentially. Non-US GAAP opex $885 million (including the acquired NXP MEMS sensor business and a one-off supplier settlement); Q2 2026 non-US GAAP net opex expected at $950-$960 million. GAAP operating income $70 million including $71 million of impairment, restructuring and phase-out costs; GAAP net income $37 million ($0.04 diluted EPS); non-US GAAP net income $122 million. Net cash from operating activities $534 million; net capex $362 million (vs $530 million a year earlier). Inventory $3.17 billion, 140 days, in line with expectation. FY2026 net opex including the NXP MEMS business (about $50 million additional expenses) and exchange rate: up low double-digit versus 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: net capex $362 million; Q2 opex $950-$960 million; inventory $3.17 billion (140 days)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Lorenzo Grandi on the gross-margin bridge: the selected price increases are 'not a price increase for what concerns us across all, let's say, customers and products', and pricing is 'quite neutral' to the Q1-to-Q2 gross margin ('it is not a booster, but it's not even a detractor'); positives are mix and lower unused capacity charges ('Our fabs are better loaded'); the main detractor is temporary suboptimal manufacturing efficiency while moving from 200mm to 300mm and silicon carbide from 150mm to 200mm. Gross margin to improve sequentially Q1 through Q4 and versus last year; unused capacity charges 'will not completely disappear' (legacy technology); transition benefits come 'mainly in 2027 more than in 2026'; capacity reservation fees much lower, without significant variation Q2-Q4; H2 may bring 'a little bit higher input cost for our manufacturing'. 'You will see a progressive improvement in our gross margin moving Q3 and Q4, and then of course in 2027.'

CEO Jean-Marc Chery on the shape of 2026: Q1 bookings showed 'absolutely no pull in order', a well-balanced quarter-to-quarter loading - 'Great confidence level to have H2 versus H1 at the usual seasonality.' Automotive grows in 2026 in ADAS, sensors (boosted by the NXP MEMS acquisition) and silicon carbide; industrial 'solid and strong growth on general purpose microcontroller'; personal electronics engaged programs contribute 'but not a big one in H2' given a change of profile in new-device introduction; data center shows strong demand acceleration including cloud optical interconnect (PIC100, BiCMOS) plus general purpose MCUs, analog and power discrete; AI infrastructure and low Earth orbit satellites 'will be very strong contributor to the performance of ST in 2026.' Asked whether, excluding personal electronics, the big programs (silicon carbide, photonics, satellites) grow quarter-on-quarter through the year, the CEO answered: 'Of course, excluding personal electronics. This is what we expect.' Q2 revenues expected 'well above average seasonality'; the outlook includes no impact from further tariff changes.

CEO Jean-Marc Chery on AI data-center strategy: 'AWS will be a fantastic driver for ST for the growth of the revenue during the next 3-5 years. Our ambition is well above, thanks to our product portfolio.' The power-flow portfolio spans SPS, low voltage MOSFETs, microcontrollers, drivers and sensing; ST is 'capable to provide on this infrastructure from a photonics solution, MEMS solution that will come pretty soon, microcontroller definitively, power switches, power drivers, controllers'. On AI data-center revenue: 'I really confirm that 2026 will show a significant breakthrough in our revenue linked to AI data center.' Marco Cassis: the expanded power portfolio (silicon, silicon carbide with different voltages and new packages, GaN) now covers 'from grid up to driving the GPUs' and 'will translate in revenues during 2026, but mainly during 2027'.

CEO Jean-Marc Chery on silicon photonics: 'Clearly on photonics and associated technology, we are in a ramp-up mode.' PIC100 is not a standard product - 'Maybe application standard specific, maybe yes.' 'You will have many innovation coming in the optical cable and optical solution. Again, the near-package optics, the co-packaged optics, all this will come and maybe faster than expected. Silicon photonics is the key enabler of all these technologies.'

CEO Jean-Marc Chery on Q1 design activity: automotive design wins across electric, hybrid and traditional vehicles in onboard chargers, DC/DC converters, power train, active suspension and vehicle control electronics (power semiconductors, smart power, automotive MCUs, analog, sensors); industrial design wins across industrial automation and robotics, building automation, power systems, healthcare and home appliances. ST 'announced support for motion sensing and secure wireless technology on Qualcomm Technologies' newly launched personal AI platform based on ST smart sensor and secure NFC controllers.' Balance-sheet inventory increased slightly in Q1 while distribution inventories were worked down.
